plan.title: Treatment x time interaction in 2x2 bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the treatment effect differ between the two time points — is an interaction question on a 2 conditions x 2 time points design with 3 replicates per cell (12 samples, 12000 gene-symbol rows in counts.csv, Salmon-derived raw integer counts, human cell line, single batch). The plan therefore fits one DESeq2 model with condition, time, and their interaction, and tests the interaction coefficient directly; it does not compare two separately-run DE analyses, which is the common and invalid substitute.

Step T1S1 does sample structure QC first (blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes), because with 3 replicates per cell a single mis-grouped sample can dominate an interaction coefficient, and the design profile reports a single batch so any structure that is not condition or time is either a technical artefact or an outlier. T1S2 is the inference step: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, ~ condition + time + condition:time with explicitly set reference levels, Wald test on the interaction term as the primary result, plus the two simple effects (treatment vs control at t0, and at t1) as named contrasts, ashr shrinkage for the reported and ranked fold changes, BH within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. T1S3 assembles the report: the three results side by side (simple effect at t0, simple effect at t1, interaction contrast), MA and dispersion diagnostics, p-value histograms, and an explicit power statement.

The honest constraint on this design is power. An interaction coefficient is a difference of two differences, so its standard error exceeds that of either simple effect at the same replicate number; at n=3 per cell, benchmark work finds only a minority of true DE genes, mostly large fold changes. The plan keeps alpha at 0.05 rather than loosening it, states the power limit, and requires that genes absent from the interaction list are NOT reported as having equal effects at both time points. T1S4 is an optional robustness check with edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same counts and design, reporting the overlap as the high-confidence set — not the union. No enrichment step is planned: the question does not ask for pathways, and adding one would be unasked scope.
